title: SIU rules on police shooting at Lac Seul First Nations community
article: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit concluded three members of the OPP's Emergency Response Team acted lawfully in the shooting death of a 39-year-old Whitefish Bay man in May.

The emergency response team was dispatched to the Lac Seul First Nations community, near Sioux Lookout, responding to reports an "intoxicated and volatile" Brian Gray shot and killed George Carpenter in his own home, said an SIU release.
Gray then took six hostages in Carpenter's home and held the gun to his own head, the release said. One woman was treated on scene for a gunshot wound to her hand.
Gray exited the home around 9:30 holding a rifle to the head of another man and refused to comply with "numerous" demands to drop the firearm.
Gray fired a shot into the air and the hostage fell to the ground, prompting three officers to fire several times, said the release.
Still conscious and moving, Gray was cuffed and taken by ambulance to a hospital in Sioux Lookout where he died from his injuries.

"In my view, the subject officers were collectively and individually justified in the use of lethal force leading to the demise of Mr. Gray in these circumstances," SIU director Ian Scott said in a release. "He had already proven himself to be violent and unpredictable in the events leading up to his death."
The SIU is an independent body called on to investigate death, serious injury or sexual assault involving a police officer and the public.
